name: Charters Towers Stock Exchange Arcade
scope: Standing Royal Arcade at 76 Mosman Street, including its projecting street canopy, paired masonry shop ranges, open passage and glazed steel central vault.
era: Present heritage arcade, with retained 1888 architectural form interpreted from the 1891 archive photograph and standing structure descriptions.

references.caption:
Charters Towers Stock Exchange, 1891
A scene in Mosman Street outside the Stock Exchange during a brief speculation boom in October 1891. [Description supplied with photograph] Other buildings visible include Harry Jeff's Mining Exchange Hotel, J. Sheen - taylor, and J. Moore's hairdressing establishment. A horse and carriage appear in the street.

The stock exchange building began life in 1888 as the Royal Arcade. It was converted into a stock exchange in 1890. [Information taken from: Don Roderick, Charters Towers and its Stock Exchange, 1977].

originalReview.notes: The State Library’s 1891 Mosman Street photograph identifies the original street entry. Visible are the projecting central barrel canopy with radial glazing, iron posts, bands of corrugated veranda roofing, and the adjacent masonry bays. Neighboring storefronts and the busy street scene do not inform the building.

review.method: Exact Qualla State Library of Queensland archive photograph, National Trust descriptions and surveyed map outline
review.notes: Started with the published Qualla gallery. Exact public-domain 1891 SLQ street photograph retained. Used the owner’s current written architectural description for the existing roof and decorated passage and the native named OSM outline for plan scale.
